system.name: TextSpan decomposition of CLIP-ViT
system.one_liner: Decompose CLIP's image representation into contributions of patches, layers and attention heads and label each part with text from CLIP's own text space.

content.variant_note: a strip showing the decomposition grid, then three coloured result panels with real examples; the tints of the grid match the panel banners
content.argues: CLIP's image representation is a sum over image tokens, layers and heads whose parts can be described in text: head roles, regions per prompt, and regions per head direction.
content.subject: An input photo passing through a CLIP-ViT token grid to the image representation, and three views of its decomposition shown on a pyramid photo.

lessons.what_to_learn: Tie a schematic to its result panels by colour: tint a column, a row and their crossing cell in a grid of tokens, and give each result panel a banner in the matching tint, so the reader sees which slice of the model each panel interprets; reuse one photo across all heat-map tiles so the comparison is immediate.
lessons.suits: Interpretability or analysis papers that split a model's output into parts (heads, tokens, layers) and show what each part contributes on shared examples.

evidence: By decomposing CLIP’s image representation as a sum across individual image patches, model layers, and attention heads
the regions with triangles are the primary contributors to a direction that is labeled as isosceles triangle

summary: The paper decomposes CLIP-ViT's image representation into a sum over image patches, layers and attention heads and uses CLIP's text space to describe each part. Figure 1 is a 2 x 2 grid split by dashed rules. The top-left strip passes an input photo of pyramids through a grid of rounded token squares (tokens by layers x heads) and a green projection layer to the image representation, with one column tinted yellow, one row purple and their crossing cell orange. Three lettered panels with banners in the same tints show results: (a) numbered text lists for a number, a shape and a color head, (b) heat maps for A photo of a pyramid and A photo of a camel, (c) joint heat maps for An isosceles triangle and Image with an orange color.
summary_zh: 论文把 CLIP-ViT 的图像表示拆成图像块、层和注意力头之和，并用文本解释各部分。图分四格：左上是 token 网格，黄紫橙三色标出头、token 及交叉；(a)(b)(c) 同色面板给出头的文字描述和两种热力图。
notes: The prior counted 3 panels; I count 4 because the top-left strip is a cell bounded by dashed rules, though it has no letter. The digest lists 9 placed bitmaps for 5 different images, so each heat-map tile is probably the photo plus a separate overlay bitmap. The three tints in the grid and the banners match by colour; the paper text does not state this mapping, it is read from the figure.
